title: Thoreau close
hook: our weeks at Walden end where he began: I went to the woods

segments.voice: Yesterday, keep one: simplicity, wildness, conscience or attention to the small. Which one went in your bag, and did you do one thing for it? Day one thousand two hundred sixty-one.

"I lived there two years and two months." That's how Thoreau sums up his stay at Walden, early in the book, almost in passing. Then he adds that he's a sojourner in civilized life again. A short stay, and then back to town. Our own stay with him has been a few weeks of mornings: a cabin, a pond, a jail, a mountain, a shore, a journal, a friend's honest tribute. Today we close the door on the cabin, and we do it with the sentence that opened it.
screen: `TWO YEARS AND TWO MONTHS.` → `BACK TO TOWN.` → `THE SENTENCE THAT OPENED IT.`

segments.voice: Here it is, from the second chapter of Walden: "I went to the woods because I wished to live deliberately, to front only the essential facts of life, and see if I could not learn what it had to teach, and not, when I came to die, discover that I had not lived." First, deliberately. Not by accident, not by habit, not because everyone else was doing it. On purpose. Second, the essential facts. To front them means to face them, head-on. Not the news, not the gossip, not the shopping. What is actually basic: food, shelter, work, the seasons, other people, death. Third, learn what it had to teach. He went as a student, not a conqueror. The woods were the teacher. Every chapter we read was a lesson he took down: the pond's depth, the ant war, the thawing bank, contact on the mountain. Fourth, he left. In the last chapter he writes, "I left the woods for as good a reason as I went there." He doesn't say the experiment failed. He says he had other lives to live. That matters, because this path isn't asking anyone to move to a cabin. The woods weren't the point. Living deliberately was. You can go to the woods for an hour on a Saturday, or for ten minutes in a city park, or by stepping outside to look at the sky before bed. Thoreau's books are an open door, not a fence. And tomorrow, a new road opens: what happens when people who meditate sit down with people who measure the mind.
screen: `TO LIVE DELIBERATELY.` · `FRONT THE ESSENTIAL FACTS.` · `THE WOODS AS TEACHER.` · then, large: `I LEFT THE WOODS.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: plan your hour outdoors. Sit, and breathe. Picture a place you could actually reach this week: a park, a path, a backyard, a riverbank, a quiet street with trees. See yourself there for an hour, with nowhere to be. No headphones, no goal. Just walking, or sitting, or watching. Ask Thoreau's question quietly: what might it have to teach? Then pick the day, and hold the picture until the bell. The bell holds the time.
Thoreau close. The end of our weeks with him, where he began: I went to the woods because I wished to live deliberately. Today's word.
Your line: go to the woods. This week, spend one hour outdoors on purpose, and let the place teach you something. Day one thousand two hundred sixty-one.

howItsDone: Some readers who finish Walden take from it a habit of going outdoors on purpose, for an hour or an afternoon, to live a little more deliberately rather than to move to a cabin.

fork.setup: you've lived in the woods for two years and learned a great deal. what do you do now?
options: stay forever, or it was all for nothing.
leave, for as good a reason as you came.
burn the cabin and forget it.
fork.reveal: Thoreau left, and said it was for as good a reason as he went there. he had other lives to live.

trapdoor: what you thought: Thoreau's lesson is to move to a cabin in the woods.
what it means: the woods were the teacher; the point was to live deliberately.
what a scholar hears: Walden opens and closes with leaving: two years and two months, and then I left the woods for as good a reason.

notes: Confirm exact wording of all three Walden quotations.

Index hook was 'forty-two days at Walden', which reads as the length of this lesson block rather than Thoreau's stay; the script uses Walden's own 'two years and two months' and calls our stay 'a few weeks of mornings'. Owner may want the index hook revised.
'Sojourner in civilized life again' is paraphrased from the same opening paragraph of Economy.
'Almost none of us are moving to a cabin' is a light general remark; soften if needed.
Last day of Block D; tomorrow opens Block E (contemplative science). The close teases it without teaching it.
Editor pass: replaced the sweeping 'almost none of us are moving to a cabin' with 'this path isn't asking anyone to move to a cabin'.
